scope: India first. Bottom-up from official counts. Student use is free, so revenue comes only from labs and teams.

source.name: All India Survey on Higher Education 2021-22, Ministry of Education
source.section: 2.2.7.1 Engineering and Technology Stream; colleges by specialisation
source.note: Read from this hosted copy of the ministry report because education.gov.in refused automated access. Report page 23, Figure 20, and the colleges section.
source.colleges_base: 2,610 of 42,825 responding colleges are specialised in Engineering & Technology. Universities and non-responding colleges are not counted.

annual_lab_licence_inr.reason: Placeholder price for the free-for-students, paid-for-labs hypothesis. No customer has seen this price.

first_stage_college_share.reason: Placeholder reach for the first three years. Not based on adoption data.

funnel.sam: Electrical, electronics and mechanical students, the branches that design battery systems
funnel.som: Assumed 5% of engineering colleges buying one lab licence

limits: Counts size the audience. They do not show willingness to pay. Enrolment is 2021-22. A Lok Sabha reply reported in August 2026 puts engineering enrolment at 62.17 lakh for 2023-24, which uses a wider definition and is secondary here.
